0.long_answer: The immune marker used for diagnosing certain subtypes of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is the HLA-B27 antigen. HLA-B27 is part of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) located on chromosome 6 and is commonly tested for in patients suspected of having an immune-mediated arthritic condition, especially in the enthesitis-related subtype of JIA. Its presence may help support the diagnosis in the appropriate clinical context.
